intent.raw_query: Morocco Marrakech and Sahara, $1000 solo, 7 days, March 2026

selected_hotel.name: Aegean Bliss Resort, Morocco (Marrakech and Sahara)

experiences.name: Explore Djemaa el-Fna Square
experiences.description: Immerse yourself in the beating heart of Marrakech at this UNESCO-listed square. Watch snake charmers, storytellers, acrobats, and musicians perform as the sun sets. Sample street food like harira soup, msemen flatbread, and freshly squeezed orange juice from the surrounding stalls.

experiences.name: Camel Trek and Overnight Desert Camp in Erg Chebbi
experiences.description: Ride a camel into the towering golden dunes of the Sahara at sunset and spend the night in a traditional Berber camp under a canopy of stars. Enjoy a campfire dinner with tagine, mint tea, and live Gnawa music. Wake at dawn to witness a breathtaking Sahara sunrise over the dunes.

experiences.name: Guided Tour of the Medina and Historic Souks
experiences.description: Navigate the labyrinthine medieval alleyways of Marrakech's ancient Medina with a knowledgeable local guide. Visit the 16th-century Ben Youssef Madrasa, the Bahia Palace, and the vibrant souks selling spices, leather goods, lanterns, and handwoven carpets. Learn about the city's rich Saadian and Almoravid history.

experiences.name: Sandboarding on the Sahara Dunes
experiences.description: Strap a board to your feet and carve down the steep, silky slopes of the Erg Chebbi mega-dunes for an adrenaline-pumping desert adventure. Local guides provide boards and instruction, and you can combine the activity with a quad bike ride across the surrounding desert plains for extra thrills.

experiences.name: Traditional Moroccan Cooking Class
experiences.description: Join a local chef in a riad kitchen for a hands-on cooking class where you learn to prepare authentic Moroccan dishes such as chicken tagine with preserved lemon, couscous with seven vegetables, and bastilla. Begin with a guided visit to the spice souk to select fresh ingredients, and finish by dining on the meal you've created on a rooftop terrace.

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Morocco (Marrakech and Sahara)
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

hotel.name: Aegean Bliss Resort, Morocco (Marrakech and Sahara)

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled - flight arrives at 13:00
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Marrakech Menara Airport at 13:00. Clear customs and collect luggage. Take the 19 bus or a shared petit taxi (negotiate fare, ~50-70 MAD) to your accommodation at Aegean Bliss Resort. Check in, freshen up, and rest briefly. Take a gentle orientation walk around your immediate neighborhood to get your bearings and exchange currency at a local bureau de change for the best rates.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Djemaa el-Fna Square (the main square), a UNESCO-listed cultural space that comes alive at dusk. Watch street performers, snake charmers, and storytellers for free. Browse the outdoor food stalls for your first authentic Moroccan meal — try a bowl of harira soup (10-15 MAD) and fresh-squeezed orange juice (4-5 MAD). Explore the edges of the medina souks as they wind down for the night.

meals.breakfast: Eat on the plane or grab a snack at the airport upon arrival
meals.lunch: Skip or grab a quick sandwich/msemen flatbread from a street vendor near the airport or hotel (~15-20 MAD)
meals.dinner: Djemaa el-Fna food stalls — harira soup, kefta skewers, and Moroccan bread for under 60 MAD total

day_by_day.notes: Day 1 is intentionally light given the afternoon arrival. Avoid aggressive touts near the square — politely decline and keep moving. Keep your valuables secure in a money belt. The Djemaa el-Fna stalls are busiest and most atmospheric between 7-10pm. March weather in Marrakech is mild and pleasant (18-24°C), ideal for evening walks.

day_by_day.morning: Start early with a traditional Moroccan breakfast at a local cafe near the medina — café au lait, msemen, honey, and amlou (almond-argan paste) for 25-35 MAD. Visit the Koutoubia Mosque and its gardens (exterior only for non-Muslims, free). Walk through the Mellah (Jewish quarter) and explore the historic Bahia Palace (70 MAD entry), a stunning 19th-century riad palace with intricate zellij tilework and carved cedar ceilings.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Saadian Tombs (70 MAD entry), a beautifully preserved 16th-century royal necropolis. Wander through the souks of the medina — the leather souk (Chouara tannery area), spice market (Rahba Kedima), and the lantern and carpet souks. Practice your bargaining skills. Visit the free Ben Youssef Madrasa (exterior area) and the surrounding neighbourhood. Grab a freshly squeezed orange juice from a street cart (5 MAD).
day_by_day.evening: Return to Djemaa el-Fna for sunset. Climb to a rooftop cafe terrace (Cafe de France or Cafe Glacier) for a mint tea with panoramic views of the square (~25-30 MAD for tea). Have dinner at a local restaurant inside the medina — try a traditional tagine with bread at a non-tourist local eatery for 50-80 MAD.

meals.breakfast: Local medina cafe — msemen, coffee, and honey for 25-35 MAD
meals.lunch: Souk street food — merguez sandwich, briouats (fried pastries), and fresh juice for under 40 MAD
meals.dinner: Local medina restaurant — lamb or vegetable tagine with Moroccan bread and mint tea for 60-90 MAD

day_by_day.notes: Book Bahia Palace and Saadian Tombs tickets in advance online to avoid queues. Wear comfortable walking shoes — medina streets are uneven. The tanneries are best viewed from rooftop leather shops; you may be pressured to buy but it is not mandatory. A combined museum pass (Marrakech Museum Pass) covering multiple sites can save money if planning multiple visits.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Majorelle Garden (70 MAD entry, or 30 MAD for the garden only without the Berber Museum), a stunning botanical garden with cobalt-blue accents created by Jacques Majorelle and later owned by Yves Saint Laurent. Arrive right at opening (8am) to beat the crowds. Alternatively, visit the free Cyber Park Arsat Moulay Abdeslam gardens for a budget option. Explore the Gueliz (New City) neighbourhood — a pleasant contrast to the medina with French colonial architecture.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a free self-guided walk through the Palmeraie (palm grove) on the outskirts of Marrakech — accessible by local bus No. 1 (4 MAD). Explore the Musée de Marrakech inside a beautifully restored 19th-century palace (50 MAD entry) with exhibitions on Moroccan art and history. Visit the attached Ben Youssef Madrasa (50 MAD, or combined ticket 70 MAD), one of the largest Islamic colleges in North Africa with breathtaking Moorish architecture.
day_by_day.evening: Take a cooking class experience — many riads offer budget group classes (150-250 MAD) where you learn to make tagine or couscous and eat your creation. Alternatively, explore the night market atmosphere of Djemaa el-Fna again and try different street foods. Visit a hammam (traditional bathhouse) for a local experience — public hammams cost as little as 15-20 MAD (bring your own kessa scrub mitt and savon beldi soap).

meals.breakfast: At your accommodation or a nearby patisserie — croissant, coffee, and fresh-squeezed juice for 20-30 MAD
meals.lunch: Cheap local eatery in Gueliz — a set lunch menu (menu du jour) at a local restaurant for 60-80 MAD including salad, main, and drink
meals.dinner: Cook your own meal if you did the cooking class, or street food at Djemaa el-Fna for 50-70 MAD

day_by_day.notes: Majorelle Garden is very popular — arrive early or book timed entry online. The public hammam experience is authentic and extremely budget-friendly but can feel overwhelming for first-timers; look for hammams with a sign saying 'bain maure' and ask your hotel for a recommendation of a clean, reputable local one. March is a great time to visit gardens as flowers are blooming.

day_by_day.date: Day 4 - 2027-03-18 (Travel Day: Marrakech to Sahara Desert)
day_by_day.morning: Wake up very early (5:00-5:30am) for a pre-arranged budget group shared minibus/CTM bus toward Ouarzazate and Merzouga (the Sahara). Book this in advance through your accommodation or a local agency — a shared group desert tour departing Marrakech typically costs 350-600 MAD per person for a 2-day/1-night trip. The route crosses the spectacular Tizi n'Tichka mountain pass (2,260m) in the High Atlas Mountains. Stop at a Berber village viewpoint for photos.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the journey through Ouarzazate (the 'Hollywood of Morocco') — stop briefly to view the exterior of Aït Benhaddou, a UNESCO World Heritage ksar (fortified village) used in films like Gladiator and Game of Thrones. Entry to the ksar is approximately 10 MAD. Continue driving through the Draa Valley past kasbahs, date palms, and dramatic desert landscapes toward Merzouga and the Erg Chebbi dunes.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at the desert camp near Merzouga at dusk. Mount camels for a 45-60 minute sunset camel trek into the Sahara dunes (usually included in tour packages). Watch the spectacular Saharan sunset from atop the orange-gold dunes of Erg Chebbi. Arrive at your desert camp — a traditional Berber nomad-style camp with shared tents, blankets, and lanterns. Enjoy a communal dinner around a campfire with live Gnawa music and drumming.

meals.breakfast: Quick breakfast at accommodation before 5am departure — bread, jam, and coffee or buy from a bakery en route
meals.lunch: Packed lunch or stop at a roadside Berber cafe in the Atlas Mountains — tagine or sandwich for 50-80 MAD
meals.dinner: Traditional Berber dinner included at the desert camp — couscous, tagine, mint tea, and fresh bread around the campfire

day_by_day.notes: Book your Sahara tour at least 2-3 days in advance. Compare prices between agencies — a reputable 2-day/1-night shared group tour including transport, camel ride, camp accommodation, and meals should cost 700-1,200 MAD per person. Bring warm layers as desert nights in March can drop to 5-10°C. Pack a headlamp, sunscreen, sunglasses, and a scarf for dust. The journey from Marrakech to Merzouga is approximately 9-10 hours total.

day_by_day.morning: Wake before sunrise (around 6:00am) to climb the Erg Chebbi dunes on foot for a breathtaking Saharan sunrise — one of the most memorable experiences in Morocco, completely free once at the camp. Watch the dunes shift from deep purple to golden orange as the sun rises over the desert. Take a short camel or walk back to camp for a Berber breakfast. Explore the surroundings of Merzouga village — visit a local nomad family (often arranged by camp guides) to learn about desert life.
day_by_day.afternoon: Begin the return journey toward Marrakech via a different scenic route if your tour offers it, potentially through the Todra Gorge (dramatic limestone canyon, free to walk through) or Dades Valley. Stop at roadside argan oil cooperatives (free to visit, no obligation to buy) to see how argan oil is traditionally produced by Berber women. Continue through the dramatic Draa Valley landscapes.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive back in Marrakech by late evening (around 9-10pm). Check back into your accommodation. Have a light late dinner near the medina or pick up street food. Rest and recover from the long travel day.

meals.breakfast: Berber breakfast at desert camp — included in tour package (bread, olive oil, honey, eggs, mint tea)
meals.lunch: Roadside Berber restaurant stop en route — tagine set menu for 60-80 MAD
meals.dinner: Light street food near accommodation upon return to Marrakech — msemen, harira, or a sandwich for 30-50 MAD

day_by_day.notes: The sunrise over the Sahara is the highlight of the entire trip — set multiple alarms and do not miss it. Bring extra water for the dune climb. If you have extra time in Merzouga, sandboarding down the dunes is a fun free activity (boards sometimes available at camp). Keep your camera protected from sand. The return journey is long — bring entertainment, snacks, and stay hydrated.

day_by_day.morning: Sleep in to recover from the desert journey. Late breakfast at a local cafe. Visit the Musée Yves Saint Laurent Marrakech (100 MAD entry) adjacent to Majorelle Garden — a beautifully designed museum celebrating the fashion designer's connection to Morocco. Alternatively, for a free option, explore the El Badi Palace ruins (70 MAD entry) — a vast 16th-century palace complex with panoramic rooftop views and resident storks nesting on the walls.
day_by_day.afternoon: Dedicate the afternoon to serious souk shopping for souvenirs — the medina souks are the budget traveler's paradise. Best buys include leather babouche slippers (60-120 MAD), argan oil (genuine, from cooperatives), spices, Berber jewelry, and handwoven textiles. Always bargain — start at 30-40% of the asking price. Visit the Mellah spice market for the best prices on saffron, ras el hanout, and cumin. Take a free self-guided walk through the Kasbah neighbourhood.
day_by_day.evening: Treat yourself to a proper hammam and traditional kessa scrub treatment at a mid-range hammam (150-250 MAD for the full treatment — a worthwhile splurge). Afterward, have a farewell Marrakech dinner at a rooftop restaurant in the medina — many offer atmospheric settings with medina views at reasonable prices. Try pastilla (sweet pigeon or chicken pie) as a special Moroccan dish.

meals.breakfast: Sleep in — late breakfast at accommodation or a local cafe for 30-40 MAD
meals.lunch: Souk lunch — a traditional Moroccan salad spread and bread at a local workers' restaurant for 40-60 MAD
meals.dinner: Rooftop medina restaurant — pastilla starter and lamb tagine for 100-150 MAD (a slight budget splurge for the last full evening)

day_by_day.notes: When bargaining in the souks, be friendly and patient — it is a cultural exchange, not a confrontation. Walk away if the price is not right; sellers will often call you back with a better offer. Genuine saffron is expensive (real Moroccan saffron costs at least 30-50 MAD per gram) — be wary of very cheap 'saffron.' The hammam is an essential Moroccan cultural experience and great for sore muscles after the desert trip.

day_by_day.morning: Enjoy a final traditional Moroccan breakfast — visit a local bakery (farran) to buy fresh-baked khobz bread, then pick up honey, cheese, and olives from a market stall to create your own spread for under 30 MAD. Take a final peaceful morning walk through the medina before the tourist crowds arrive. Visit any remaining sites on your list — the Almoravid Koubba (the only surviving Almoravid-era structure in Marrakech, 20 MAD entry) is small but historically significant. Buy any last-minute souvenirs.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check out of accommodation (store luggage if needed). Enjoy a final mint tea at a medina cafe. Head to the airport — allow at least 2 hours before departure. Take the 19 bus (4 MAD) or negotiate a shared taxi to the airport. Reflect on an incredible week of culture, history, desert adventure, and Moroccan hospitality.
day_by_day.evening: Departure — flight home. Safe travels!

meals.breakfast: DIY market breakfast — fresh bread, olives, honey, and coffee for under 30 MAD
meals.lunch: Final medina lunch — a bowl of harira soup with bread and a fresh orange juice for 25-35 MAD
meals.dinner: Airport or in-flight meal

day_by_day.notes: Allow extra time for airport check-in — Marrakech Menara Airport can be busy. Keep some MAD for final transport and any airport purchases but note that unused Moroccan dirhams cannot easily be exchanged outside Morocco, so spend or exchange remaining cash before departure. Take photos of any receipts and souvenir purchases in case of customs questions. The total estimated budget for 7 days (excluding flights) is approximately 3,500-5,000 MAD (~$350-500 USD) per person including accommodation, transport, meals, entry fees, and the Sahara tour.

trip_options.title: Classic Morocco (Marrakech and Sahara) Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

hotel.name: Aegean Bliss Resort, Morocco (Marrakech and Sahara)

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Marrakech Menara Airport at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Transfer to Aegean Bliss Resort and check in. Freshen up and orient yourself with the property and surroundings.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a gentle introductory stroll through the nearby Gueliz (Ville Nouvelle) neighborhood to get your bearings. Visit the Majorelle Garden (Jardin Majorelle) — a stunning cobalt-blue botanical garden co-restored by Yves Saint Laurent. Explore the on-site Berber Museum for a first taste of Moroccan culture and history.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Djemaa el-Fna square as the sun sets to experience the world-famous open-air spectacle: snake charmers, musicians, storytellers, and food stalls lighting up the night. Soak in the atmosphere and enjoy your first evening in Marrakech.

meals.breakfast: Meal on the plane or light snack at the airport upon arrival
meals.lunch: Café de France or a simple café terrace overlooking Djemaa el-Fna for a quick Moroccan sandwich (merguez or kefta) and fresh orange juice (~80–120 MAD)
meals.dinner: Dinner at one of the iconic Djemaa el-Fna food stalls — try harira soup, grilled brochettes, and Moroccan salads for an authentic and affordable experience (~100–150 MAD)

day_by_day.notes: Day 1 activities only begin after 13:00 arrival. Keep the afternoon light to recover from travel. Exchange currency at the airport or a bureau de change in Gueliz for better rates than hotels.

day_by_day.morning: Deep dive into Marrakech's historic Medina. Start at the Koutoubia Mosque (exterior) — the city's iconic 12th-century minaret. Then explore the Ben Youssef Medersa, a breathtaking 14th-century Islamic college with intricate zellij tilework, carved cedar wood, and stucco plasterwork. Arrive early to beat the crowds.
day_by_day.afternoon: Wander through the labyrinthine souks of the Medina — explore the spice souk, leather tanneries, carpet bazaars, and lantern markets. Visit the Bahia Palace, a stunning 19th-century riad-style palace with ornate painted ceilings and lush courtyard gardens. Bargain for a handcrafted souvenir in the artisan quarter.
day_by_day.evening: Attend a traditional Moroccan cooking class or visit a riad rooftop for sunset views over the Medina. Enjoy a relaxed evening in the Mellah (Jewish quarter) and stroll through the covered Mellah market.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the resort or a local café — traditional Moroccan spread: msemen (flatbread), amlou (almond-argan dip), honey, mint tea (~60–100 MAD)
meals.lunch: Lunch at Café des Épices in the spice square — tagine or couscous with a view of the rooftops (~120–180 MAD)
meals.dinner: Dinner at Le Foundouk or a mid-range riad restaurant in the Medina — try bastilla (pigeon pie) or lamb tagine with prunes and almonds (~200–300 MAD)

day_by_day.notes: Wear comfortable walking shoes for the Medina's cobblestone streets. Hire a licensed guide from the tourist office for the souk tour to avoid aggressive touts (~200–300 MAD for a half-day). Ben Youssef Medersa entry ~70 MAD.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to the Atlas Mountains and Berber villages. Depart early by shared minibus or private transfer toward the Ourika Valley (~45 min from Marrakech). Trek through terraced Berber farmland, cross a river gorge, and hike to the Setti Fatma waterfalls (a series of seven cascading falls accessible via a short guided hike).
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit a traditional Berber family home for a mint tea ceremony and learn about mountain life and argan oil production. Explore the weekly Ourika market if visiting on Monday. Enjoy the stunning Atlas backdrop and fresh mountain air before returning to Marrakech by late afternoon.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Marrakech and relax at the resort. Optional: visit a traditional hammam for a rejuvenating steam bath and kessa scrub — a quintessential Moroccan wellness ritual.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the resort before departure (~included or ~80 MAD at a local café)
meals.lunch: Riverside lunch at a local Ourika Valley restaurant — fresh trout from the river, Moroccan salads, and bread (~120–180 MAD)
meals.dinner: Casual dinner near the hotel in Gueliz — try Comptoir Darna for a mid-range Moroccan-French fusion meal or a neighborhood restaurant (~180–250 MAD)

day_by_day.notes: Book a shared day-trip transfer from Djemaa el-Fna or through your hotel (~150–250 MAD per person shared). Wear layers — Atlas mornings can be cool in March. The hammam experience costs ~150–300 MAD at a mid-range establishment.

day_by_day.morning: Depart Marrakech early for the Sahara Desert via the scenic Draa Valley route (private or shared transfer, approximately 8–9 hours with stops). Cross the High Atlas Mountains through the dramatic Tizi n'Tichka pass (2,260m elevation) with breathtaking panoramic views and photo stops.
day_by_day.afternoon: Stop in Ouarzazate — the 'Hollywood of Morocco' — to visit the Aït Benhaddou UNESCO World Heritage ksar (fortified village), one of the most iconic earthen architecture sites in the world, used in films like Gladiator and Game of Thrones. Explore the kasbahs and climb to the top for sweeping desert valley views.
day_by_day.evening: Continue driving through the Draa Valley, passing palm oases and ancient kasbahs, arriving at your desert camp near Merzouga or Zagora by early evening. Welcome mint tea at the camp, then mount a camel for a sunset ride into the Erg Chebbi dunes. Watch the Sahara sunset paint the dunes gold and orange.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the resort before departure
meals.lunch: Lunch in Ouarzazate near Aït Benhaddou — tagine at a local restaurant with views of the ksar (~120–180 MAD)
meals.dinner: Traditional Berber dinner under the stars at the desert camp — harira, tagine, couscous, and Moroccan pastries with live Gnawa music (~included in camp package or ~200–300 MAD)

day_by_day.notes: Book a shared or private transfer in advance — shared costs ~300–500 MAD per person; private ~800–1,200 MAD. Desert camp accommodation ranges from basic nomad tents to luxury glamping. Book a mid-range camp with private tent, private bathroom, and breakfast for ~600–1,000 MAD per night. Aït Benhaddou entry ~30 MAD.

day_by_day.morning: Wake before dawn to climb the Erg Chebbi sand dunes on foot or by camel for a spectacular Sahara sunrise — one of the most memorable experiences in Morocco. The silence and shifting colors of the desert at dawn are extraordinary. Return to camp for a Berber breakfast.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the desert region: visit a nomadic Berber family encampment, learn about traditional desert life, and try sandboarding on the dunes. Alternatively, take a 4x4 excursion through the rocky desert hamada landscape to discover hidden fossil beds and remote oasis villages. Rest during the hottest part of the afternoon.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy a final sunset over the dunes and an evening of storytelling around a desert campfire with Gnawa drumming and traditional music. Stargaze in one of the darkest skies in North Africa — the Milky Way is clearly visible in March.

meals.breakfast: Berber desert breakfast at camp — khobz bread, olive oil, honey, mint tea, eggs (~included in camp package)
meals.lunch: Light lunch at the desert camp or packed lunch during the 4x4 excursion — Moroccan salads, tagine, fresh fruit (~100–150 MAD if not included)
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner at the desert camp under the stars — traditional Berber feast with live music (~included or ~200–250 MAD)

day_by_day.notes: Bring a headlamp, warm layers for cool desert nights (March nights can drop to 5–10°C), sunscreen, and a scarf for wind and sand. Sandboarding boards can be rented at the camp (~50–80 MAD). The 4x4 excursion costs approximately ~300–500 MAD per person.

day_by_day.morning: Depart the desert camp after breakfast and begin the return journey to Marrakech via the Todra Gorge route — a dramatic alternative route through towering 300-meter limestone canyon walls. Stop for a walk through the gorge and enjoy the stunning geological formations.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue through the Dadès Valley (Valley of a Thousand Kasbahs) — a scenic route lined with rose gardens, ancient fortified kasbahs, and dramatic rock formations. Stop at the Dadès Gorge viewpoint and the famous 'monkey fingers' rock formations. Optional stop at a rose cooperative (the region is famous for its May rose harvest, and cooperatives are open year-round).
day_by_day.evening: Arrive back in Marrakech by evening. Check back into the resort, freshen up, and enjoy a leisurely final evening in the city. Visit the Mellah night market or a rooftop bar in Gueliz for a relaxing nightcap.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the desert camp before departure
meals.lunch: Lunch stop at a local restaurant in Tinerhir near the Todra Gorge — fresh tagine and Berber bread (~120–160 MAD)
meals.dinner: Welcome-back dinner at a recommended Marrakech restaurant — try Al Fassia (women-run traditional Moroccan restaurant) for an authentic mid-range dinner (~250–350 MAD)

day_by_day.notes: The Todra Gorge route adds approximately 1–2 hours to the return journey but is highly recommended for the scenery. Total drive time is approximately 8–10 hours with stops. Consider splitting the return with an overnight in Tinerhir if you prefer a slower pace.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Marrakech — visit the El Badi Palace ruins, a 16th-century Saadian palace once considered one of the most magnificent in the world. Explore the stork-nesting towers and underground dungeons. Nearby, visit the Saadian Tombs — a beautifully preserved royal necropolis hidden for centuries and rediscovered in 1917.
day_by_day.afternoon: Last-minute souvenir shopping in the souks or the Ensemble Artisanal (government-run fixed-price craft center — great for fair prices without bargaining). Enjoy a final mint tea ceremony at a traditional riad café. Pack and prepare for departure.
day_by_day.evening: Transfer to Marrakech Menara Airport for your departure flight. Reflect on an incredible week of culture, desert adventure, history, and authentic Moroccan experiences.

meals.breakfast: Final Moroccan breakfast at the resort — fresh-baked msemen, honey, argan oil, mint tea, and fresh-squeezed orange juice
meals.lunch: Farewell lunch at a rooftop restaurant in the Medina with views of the Koutoubia Mosque — try a classic Moroccan couscous (traditionally served on Fridays) or pastilla (~150–200 MAD)
meals.dinner: Light meal at the airport or an early dinner near the hotel before the transfer (~100–150 MAD)

day_by_day.notes: El Badi Palace entry ~70 MAD; Saadian Tombs entry ~70 MAD. Arrive at the airport at least 2.5 hours before international departure. The Ensemble Artisanal is located in Gueliz and is ideal for last-minute quality purchases at fixed prices. Keep some MAD for airport purchases or exchange remaining currency before departure.

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Morocco (Marrakech and Sahara) Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

hotel.name: Aegean Bliss Resort, Morocco (Marrakech and Sahara)

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled – Flight LH arrives at 13:00. Private luxury transfer from Marrakech Menara Airport to Aegean Bliss Resort with a dedicated concierge greeting, chilled welcome drinks, and luggage handling.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private check-in experience at Aegean Bliss Resort. Settle into your beachfront suite, enjoy a curated welcome amenity tray with Moroccan mint tea, fresh dates, and local pastries. Take a leisurely orientation walk around the resort grounds and unwind by the pool or spa to recover from travel.
day_by_day.evening: Gentle introduction to Marrakech – a private guided evening stroll through the illuminated Djemaa el-Fna square to absorb the atmosphere of storytellers, musicians, and food stalls at dusk. Return to the resort for a relaxed first dinner.

meals.breakfast: Not applicable (in-flight or airport lounge)
meals.lunch: Not applicable – arrival at 13:00; light welcome spread at the resort upon check-in
meals.dinner: La Maison Arabe Restaurant – one of Marrakech's most celebrated fine-dining establishments offering traditional Moroccan cuisine (bastilla, slow-cooked lamb tagine, saffron couscous) in an opulent riad setting with live Gnawa music

day_by_day.notes: Arrange airport VIP meet-and-greet service in advance. Request the concierge to brief you on the week's itinerary over evening tea. Confirm all upcoming private transfers and desert camp reservations upon check-in.

day_by_day.morning: Private guided tour of the UNESCO-listed Medina of Marrakech. Explore the Koutoubia Mosque gardens, the magnificent Bahia Palace with its intricately carved cedar ceilings and zellij tilework, and the haunting ruins of the El Badi Palace. Exclusive early access arranged through a private guide to avoid crowds.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Saadian Tombs – a hidden necropolis of extraordinary craftsmanship – followed by a curated tour of the Mellah (Jewish Quarter) and its historic synagogues. Stop at the Maison de la Photographie for a rooftop mint tea with panoramic Medina views. Private souk shopping experience with a personal stylist/guide to discover artisan leather goods, spices, Berber rugs, and lanterns without the overwhelm.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cocktails on a private rooftop terrace overlooking the Medina skyline. Followed by an exclusive private dinner at a heritage riad restaurant.

meals.breakfast: Lavish Moroccan breakfast at the resort – msemen flatbreads, amlou (almond-argan dip), fresh-squeezed orange juice, Medjool dates, Berber omelette, and premium Moroccan coffee
meals.lunch: Nomad Restaurant, Marrakech – a chic rooftop eatery in the Medina offering elevated modern Moroccan cuisine with panoramic views; try the lamb mechoui and pomegranate salad
meals.dinner: Dar Yacout – legendary Marrakech riad restaurant; a theatrical multi-course feast of traditional Moroccan dishes served in candlelit courtyards with live oud music

day_by_day.notes: Wear comfortable walking shoes for Medina exploration. Dress modestly (shoulders and knees covered) when visiting religious and heritage sites. A private guide is strongly recommended for navigating the souks efficiently and authentically.

day_by_day.morning: Private early morning visit to the Majorelle Garden and the adjacent Yves Saint Laurent Museum (MYMM) before the crowds arrive. Stroll through the cobalt-blue villa and exotic botanical garden, then explore the world-class YSL retrospective exhibition. Proceed to the Musée de Marrakech for Moroccan decorative arts and Islamic manuscripts.
day_by_day.afternoon: Indulge in a traditional royal hammam and spa ritual at a premium hammam – a full black soap scrub (kessa), rhassoul clay mask, argan oil massage, and rose water treatment. Recommended: Les Bains de Marrakech or the resort spa if available. Afternoon at leisure – pool time, light reading, or optional private cooking class at a local riad kitchen learning to make tagine and bastilla.
day_by_day.evening: Private rooftop dinner under the stars with Moroccan lanterns and a curated menu. Optional: attend an exclusive Fantasia equestrian show (Tbourida) if seasonally available, showcasing Berber horsemen in traditional dress.

meals.breakfast: À la carte breakfast at the resort's garden terrace – fresh Moroccan pastries (chebakia, briouat), seasonal fruit platter, yogurt with honey and argan oil, and freshly brewed Moroccan spiced coffee
meals.lunch: Café du Livre or Pepe Nero – a refined café/restaurant in Marrakech's Gueliz district; light Mediterranean-Moroccan fusion dishes including grilled sea bass chermoula and fresh vegetable couscous
meals.dinner: Palais Namaskar or equivalent luxury resort restaurant – elegant poolside dining with a curated Moroccan-French fusion tasting menu and sommelier-selected wine pairing

day_by_day.notes: Book the Majorelle Garden and YSL Museum tickets in advance as they sell out quickly. Schedule the hammam for early afternoon (around 14:00) for maximum relaxation. The cooking class (if chosen) typically runs 2–3 hours and includes a full meal at the end.

day_by_day.date: Day 4 – March 18, 2027 (Marrakech to Sahara – Scenic Drive)
day_by_day.morning: Early departure by private luxury 4x4 vehicle on the epic Marrakech-to-Sahara road journey. Cross the High Atlas Mountains via the dramatic Tizi n'Tichka pass (2,260m elevation) with stops for panoramic mountain photography. Visit the UNESCO World Heritage site of Aït Benhaddou – the extraordinary fortified ksar (citadel) used as a film set for Gladiator, Game of Thrones, and Lawrence of Arabia. Guided exploration of the ancient mudbrick city with a local Berber guide.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue south through the Valley of Roses (Vallée du Dadès) and the Drâa Valley, passing ancient kasbahs, palm oases, and ochre-colored gorges. Stop at Ouarzazate (the 'Hollywood of Africa') for a brief visit to the Atlas Film Studios. Arrive in the Drâa Valley or Zagora area as the desert landscape opens up. Light refreshments at a traditional Berber family home en route.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at the luxury desert camp near Erg Chebbi or Erg Chigaga dunes (approximately 9–10 hours total drive with stops, or split over two days if preferred). Settle into your private luxury tent suite with en-suite bathroom, plush bedding, and Moroccan décor. Sundowner cocktails on the dunes as the sun melts into the Sahara horizon.

meals.breakfast: Early hearty breakfast at the resort before departure – Moroccan spread with eggs, pastries, fresh juice, and coffee
meals.lunch: Picnic lunch prepared by the resort – artisan sandwiches, Moroccan salads, fresh fruit, and bottled water served at a scenic Atlas Mountain viewpoint or at a kasbah restaurant in Aït Benhaddou
meals.dinner: Traditional Berber feast at the luxury desert camp – slow-roasted lamb mechoui, vegetable tagine, Moroccan salads, and fresh bread cooked in a clay oven, served under a canopy of stars with live Gnawa drumming around a campfire

day_by_day.notes: The Marrakech-to-Sahara drive is approximately 350–400km (5–6 hours driving, longer with stops). An alternative is a 1-hour private charter flight to Ouarzazate to save time if preferred. Bring layers – desert nights can be surprisingly cold in March. Confirm luxury camp reservation well in advance as top camps have limited tents.

day_by_day.morning: Pre-dawn wake-up call for a private camel trek into the Erg Chebbi or Erg Chigaga dunes to witness the legendary Sahara sunrise. Watch the golden light paint the towering sand dunes in shades of amber and crimson. Return to camp for a full Moroccan breakfast. Optional: private sandboarding session on the dunes with equipment provided by the camp.
day_by_day.afternoon: Guided 4x4 desert excursion into the deeper Sahara – visit a nomadic Berber family camp for authentic tea ceremony and storytelling about traditional desert life. Explore fossil sites and ancient rock carvings. Return to camp for a restorative afternoon – rest in your luxury tent, enjoy a desert spa treatment (hammam, argan massage), or take a private guided walk to learn desert navigation by the stars.
day_by_day.evening: Private sunset camel ride to a secluded dune peak for champagne sundowners. Return to camp for an intimate private dinner set up on the dunes under a breathtaking Saharan night sky (one of the world's best stargazing locations). Optional: private astronomer/guide for a stargazing session with telescope.

meals.breakfast: Full Moroccan breakfast at camp after sunrise camel trek – msemen, Berber omelette, honey, amlou, fresh fruit, mint tea, and coffee
meals.lunch: Leisurely lunch at the luxury camp – cold mezze spread, Moroccan salads, grilled kefta, fresh bread, and refreshing juices in the shade of the camp's lounge tent
meals.dinner: Exclusive private dinner set up on the dunes – a curated 4-course Moroccan menu with candles, lanterns, and live Gnawa music; includes traditional harira soup, bastilla, lamb tagine with prunes and almonds, and Moroccan pastries with mint tea

day_by_day.notes: March temperatures in the Sahara are pleasant during the day (20–25°C) but can drop to 5–10°C at night. Bring a warm layer for the pre-dawn camel trek. Apply high-SPF sunscreen and wear a headscarf/hat for afternoon activities. Photography opportunities are exceptional – bring a tripod for night sky shots.

day_by_day.date: Day 6 – March 20, 2027 (Sahara to Marrakech – Return Journey)
day_by_day.morning: Final sunrise over the Sahara dunes (optional short walk). Leisurely breakfast at camp. Private 4x4 transfer back toward Marrakech via a different scenic route – through the Todra Gorge, a spectacular canyon with 300-meter-high rock walls, perfect for a dramatic walk along the riverbed. Optional light hike with a local guide through the gorge.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue through the Dadès Gorge ('Valley of a Thousand Kasbahs') with photo stops at the most scenic viewpoints. Visit a traditional Berber cooperative for argan oil and rose water products – a meaningful and authentic shopping experience supporting local artisans. Arrive back in Marrakech by late afternoon. Check back into Aegean Bliss Resort, freshen up, and decompress.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell-to-the-Medina evening – a private guided night tour of Djemaa el-Fna square at its most vibrant, followed by a celebratory final dinner at one of Marrakech's most prestigious restaurants.

meals.breakfast: Final desert camp breakfast – full Moroccan spread with fresh mint tea ceremony
meals.lunch: Lunch at a scenic kasbah restaurant en route – Restaurant Tissadrine or similar in the Dadès/Todra area; traditional Berber tagine, fresh salads, and homemade bread with mountain views
meals.dinner: Le Tobsil, Marrakech – an intimate, acclaimed riad restaurant offering a lavish set Moroccan feast in a candlelit courtyard; considered one of the finest dining experiences in all of Morocco

day_by_day.notes: The return drive from Erg Chebbi is approximately 350–400km. Departing camp by 08:00–09:00 is recommended to allow comfortable driving with stops and arrival in Marrakech by 18:00–19:00. Alternatively, book a private charter flight from Ouarzazate back to Marrakech (45 minutes) to maximize the final evening in the city.

day_by_day.morning: Relaxed final morning at the resort. Optional last-minute Marrakech experience: visit the Mellah market for premium souvenir shopping – saffron, argan oil, handwoven Berber textiles, silver jewelry, and hand-painted ceramics. Alternatively, enjoy a final spa treatment or yoga session at the resort to restore and rejuvenate after the desert adventure.
day_by_day.afternoon: Farewell lunch at a scenic Marrakech rooftop restaurant. Final resort check-out with private luxury transfer to Marrakech Menara Airport. Concierge assistance with luggage and departure formalities. VIP airport lounge access arranged if available.
day_by_day.evening: Departure – flight home with memories of an extraordinary Moroccan journey spanning imperial cities, ancient kasbahs, and the timeless Sahara Desert.

meals.breakfast: Grand final breakfast at the resort – full à la carte Moroccan and continental spread; fresh-squeezed orange juice, pastries, eggs, fruit, and premium coffee on the terrace
meals.lunch: Café Arabe, Marrakech – a stylish three-floor riad restaurant with a rooftop pool terrace; Italian-Moroccan fusion menu with excellent cocktails and panoramic Medina views; perfect for a relaxed farewell meal
meals.dinner: In-flight dining or airport lounge (departure dependent on flight schedule)

day_by_day.notes: Allow at least 3 hours before your departure flight for airport transfer and check-in, especially for international flights. The concierge can arrange last-minute gift wrapping and shipping of larger souvenir purchases directly to your home address. Consider tipping your private guide, driver, and camp staff generously – a customary and appreciated gesture in Morocco.
